findings.title: No test that a valid amount pushes the confirm screen with the right amount and contact
findings.failure_scenario: Change the .continueTapped handler at SendMoneyFeature.swift:92-93 so it passes the wrong amount (for example state.balance or 0), or so it never appends confirm. Every test still passes. continueBlocked only covers the invalid case (balance 10, input 50). sendSuccess, sendFailureAndRetry and doubleTapSendsOnce put the confirm screen straight into the initial path state, so no test checks that the real amount screen produces a correct confirm screen.
findings.evidence: SendMoneyFeatureTests.swift:52-64 only sends continueTapped when canContinue is false. The test asserts nothing, so it relies on TestStore's exhaustivity to show nothing changed. SendMoneyFeature.swift:92-93 `state.path.append(.confirm(ConfirmFeature.State(contact: amount.contact, amount: amount.input.amount)))` is never reached by any test.
findings.fix: Add a test where the amount state has a valid input, e.g. "40" with balance 250. Send continueTapped and assert that path gains .confirm(ConfirmFeature.State(contact: ana, amount: 40)).
findings.verification_note: I read every test in SendMoneyFeatureTests.swift. The only test that sends .amount(.continueTapped) is continueBlocked, and it uses an amount that cannot continue (it checks !canContinue). Every confirm-screen test seeds .confirm in the initial StackState. So the append at SendMoneyFeature.swift:92-93 is never run in a test, and a mutation that passes the wrong amount or contact, or drops the push, survives. This logic lives in SendMoneyFeature's reducer, so only this file's tests can cover it. I kept major: the confirm screen would show and send the wrong amount, and nothing catches it.

findings.title: Account-load failure path and tapping a contact before the balance loads are untested
findings.failure_scenario: Two mutations survive with no test failing. First, removing the catch/log in .task: the .run closure can throw, so this still compiles, and a load error is no longer logged. Second, replacing the `guard let balance` in contactTapped with something like `state.balance ?? 0`: a contact tapped before load then pushes an amount screen with balance 0. Deleting the guard outright would not compile, because AmountFeature.State needs a non-optional balance.
findings.evidence: SendMoneyFeature.swift:73-75 (`catch { log.log(.error, "account load failed", ...) }`) and :84 (`guard let balance = state.balance else { return .none }`) have no test. taskLoads (lines 13-27) only covers success, and contactPush seeds balance: 250.
findings.fix: Add a test with accountClient.balance throwing. Assert that state is unchanged and that an error is logged. Add a test that contactTapped with balance nil leaves path empty.
findings.verification_note: I confirmed that no test overrides accountClient.balance or accountClient.contacts to throw, and no test sends contactTapped while balance is nil. Both branches (lines 73-75 and 84) are unexercised. I sharpened the scenario: removing the guard outright fails to compile, but a nil-coalescing mutation survives. I kept the severity at minor because this is a coverage gap on secondary paths with no concrete harm yet.

notes:
The three reducers are implemented; 7 tests in SendMoneyFeatureTests.swift pass and prove showed all 7 fail with the source reverted. Fix pass: ConfirmFeature `.sendTapped`/`.retryTapped` now `guard !state.isSending else { return .none }`; new test doubleTapSendsOnce covers it (accountClient.send called once). NOT fixed: the finding about a test for the amount-to-confirm push and `.keyTapped`. `AmountInput.press` and `BalanceRules.canSend` are still contract stubs (press does nothing, canSend returns false), outside this write set, so a valid-continue test cannot pass until amount-input lands; add one after merge. `@CasePathable` is on `ConfirmFeature.Action.Delegate` so tests can `receive(\.path[id:].confirm.delegate.sent)`. Failure logging uses `log.log(.error, "send failed", category: "Send", [.public("error", ...)])`. A failed account load logs "account load failed" in category "Send". `.contactTapped` does nothing while `balance` is nil.
